name: AiSOC
description: Open-source AI Security Operations Center: alert fusion, LLM-agent triage, MITRE ATT&CK investigation, and a replayable decision ledger for every agent step. Self-hostable, runs with no API keys, MIT licensed. Ships an MCP server for Claude, Cursor and Continue.
one_liner: A self-hosted AI security guard for a company's computer systems: it watches alerts from security tools, uses AI to investigate what looks suspicious, and shows a human exactly what it checked before anything gets acted on.
buyer: An IT manager at a small-to-mid-size company who needs basic security monitoring but can't afford a full enterprise security operations team or a pricey SIEM contract.
business_use_cases: A small company's one-person IT team deploys it to get automated first-pass triage on security alerts instead of manually reviewing everything.
An MSP (managed service provider) offers it as the engine behind a 'security monitoring' add-on service for multiple small-business clients.
A compliance-focused startup uses its auditable decision log to satisfy a security-review requirement without buying an expensive commercial SOC platform.

money_ideas.idea: A managed-hosting tier for companies that want the tool but not the operational burden of running it.
Paid detection-rule packs for specific industries (healthcare, fintech compliance).

steal_this: An MSP could stand this up for one existing client this weekend as a pilot 'AI-assisted monitoring' add-on and use that as the case study to sell it to the rest of their book of business.
